title: Birdcar: expertise made understandable
question: Choose the visual world for the public site, Writing, and explanatory figures. All retain the Alkaline wordmark and lead with a clear, pitch-free Walkthrough. These are direction boards, not finished page designs.

options.label: The report, unfolded
options.lineage: Exploded-view product guides: make something understandable by showing its parts and their relationships.
options.thesis: Make the value of the Walkthrough visible before someone books it.
options.viewport: A short business promise and visible booking action sit above a page-wide explanation: your working day → our conversation → the report you keep, with its three sections made readable.
options.risk: Could make the business look like it only sells reports; real implementation work must follow immediately and the diagrams must use ordinary language.

raised.raise: Use one consistent visual meaning for each line, label, and state; nothing pretends to be a measured business result.
Keep the named expert and first-person judgment present throughout, rather than making the report the whole identity.
Give the first viewport one decisive hierarchy and a confidently large invitation, not a collection of equally weighted boxes.
Direct attention to one explanatory change at a time, while the complete static explanation remains available.
Make the promised sequence and three-business-day handoff explicit instead of relying on decorative arrows.

regions.label: Where I would start / Your choice

options.label: The clear argument
options.lineage: Illustrated explanatory publications: a strong argument, a clear figure, and evidence worth reading.
options.thesis: Let visitors recognize their own business, then show why a conversation with you is useful.
options.viewport: A large recognizable business problem occupies the opening; a connected illustration beneath traces the Walkthrough into findings, recommendations, and a first step, with booking beside the explanation.
options.risk: The most familiar of these directions: editorial consulting sites are common, so specificity and the quality of the diagrams must earn its identity.

regions.label: What we discuss → what you keep
Why it helps / Book a Walkthrough
A real example of the work

options.label: Clarity, in layers
options.lineage: Layered paper-cut compositions, translated into labeled, flat-color SVG rather than floral decoration.
options.thesis: Make understanding visible as a few clear layers, built from the work people actually do.
options.viewport: A central, symmetrical layered figure connects the working day, the problems we uncover, and the report; the offer and booking action stay in an immediately readable band above it.
options.case: Matches the explanation-first goal through visible layers and excellent static reproduction; less directly associated with a technical consulting practice than the report guide.
options.risk: More playful than a conventional technical consultancy; the figure must remain a legible explanation, not a decorative badge or an interaction puzzle.

regions.label: Layered figure: context → findings → first step

options.label: Signal bench
options.thesis: Present the Walkthrough as finding a meaningful signal in everyday operational noise.
options.viewport: The operational story resolves from moving traces into labeled findings, with a booking action beside the instrument.
options.case: Loses on audience identification and offer clarity: introduces unfamiliar controls and suggests live measurement that the offer does not provide.
options.kept: Consistent meanings for every visual mark and state.
options.risk: Visitors have to understand the instrument before they understand the service.

options.label: Personal room
options.thesis: Meet the person doing the work through an explorable studio with writing and project artifacts.
options.viewport: An explorable room presents the person, writing, and work, with a plain booking link outside the scene.
options.case: Loses on audience identification and offer clarity: decorating or exploring a room adds a task to a prospect who needs to understand an engagement.
options.kept: Personal authorship should be present throughout the experience.
options.risk: A memorable personal website that delays the business decision.

options.label: Moving broadside
options.thesis: Drive a direct argument from business frustration to a concrete next step.
options.viewport: A diagonal declaration and booking wedge advance into panels explaining the Walkthrough.
options.case: Loses on audience identification and offer clarity: agitation and forced directional reading work against a pitch-free, approachable consultation.
options.kept: A decisive hierarchy rather than equally weighted content boxes.
options.risk: The visual rhetoric is more aggressive than the working relationship.

options.label: Spatial console
options.lineage: Sixth-generation console dashboards and ambient spatial menus.
options.thesis: Explore the stages of working together as luminous objects in a quiet space.
options.viewport: A few objects represent the conversation, report, and optional implementation, with a booking action outside the scene.
options.case: Loses on audience identification and offer clarity: spatial navigation obscures sequence and translates poorly into the required written and print explanations.
options.kept: One focal change at a time, without removing the complete explanation.
options.risk: Technically impressive atmosphere substitutes for evidence of useful work.

options.label: Seasonal calendar
options.lineage: Pickling journals and dated seasonal shelves.
options.thesis: Show the conversation, discovery, and report as a clearly labeled progression over time.
options.viewport: A shelf-like sequence explains the hour together and the report delivered within three business days.
options.case: Loses on audience identification and offer clarity: a culinary metaphor needs explanation and introduces stages and controls that the engagement does not have.
options.kept: Name the actual handoff and timing explicitly.
options.risk: The metaphor becomes the subject instead of the client's business.

canonCard.label: A modern B2B studio, played straight
canonCard.thesis: A familiar, carefully executed consultancy site with strong typography, work examples, and a clear booking invitation.
canonCard.viewport: A large value proposition and CTA sit beside a Walkthrough illustration, followed by proof and process.
canonCard.risk: Familiar and easy to scan, but differentiation depends mostly on the work and writing rather than the composition.
